items.followUp: Describe the role of the liver and pancreas in digestion in the small intestine.

rubric.why: Bile’s role in the small intestine is identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bile neutralizes acidic chyme or emulsifies fats; both are not required.

rubric.why: A correct pancreatic enzyme action is stated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least one correct enzyme and product pair.

rubric.why: A correct example of intestinal juice completing digestion is given.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least one correct intestinal enzyme and product pair.

rubric.why: The role of the villi in absorption is identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that villi absorb digested nutrients.

rubric.why: The routes by which the main digested nutrients enter circulation are distinguished.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glucose and amino acids enter blood capillaries while fatty acids and glycerol enter lacteals.

modelAnswer: Chyme enters the duodenum of the small intestine; bile neutralizes its acidity and emulsifies fats.
Pancreatic amylase converts starch into maltose, trypsin breaks proteins into peptides, and lipase breaks fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
Intestinal enzymes complete digestion: maltase converts maltose into glucose, and peptidases convert peptides into amino acids.
The inner lining has villi that absorb digested nutrients; glucose and amino acids enter blood capillaries, while fatty acids and glycerol enter lacteals.
Blood and lymph carry the absorbed nutrients from the small intestine to the body cells.

items.followUp: Trace the route of blood during pulmonary and systemic circulation, naming the chambers and major vessels.

rubric.why: The outgoing part of pulmonary circulation is correctly described.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for tracing deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle through the pulmonary artery to the lungs.

rubric.why: The return of oxygenated blood from the lungs is correctly described.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium through the pulmonary veins.

rubric.why: The outgoing part of systemic circulation is correctly described.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for tracing oxygenated blood from the left ventricle through the aorta to the body.

rubric.why: The return of deoxygenated blood from the body is correctly described.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that deoxygenated blood returns to the right atrium through the venae cavae.

modelAnswer: In pulmonary circulation, the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs.
In the lungs, the blood receives oxygen and returns to the left atrium through the pulmonary veins.
In systemic circulation, the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta to the rest of the body.
After delivering oxygen to the body, the deoxygenated blood returns to the right atrium through the venae cavae.

rubric.why: Histology is correctly associated with the study of tissues, particularly under a microscope.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining histology as the microscopic study of tissues.

rubric.why: Morphology is correctly associated with the form and structure of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining morphology as the study of the form and structure of organisms.

modelAnswer: Histology is the microscopic study of tissues.
Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms.

items.followUp: What are multicellular organisms, and how do their cells perform different functions?

rubric.why: The defining feature of a unicellular organism is stated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a unicellular organism consists of one cell.

rubric.why: The student explains that its single cell carries out the organism’s life activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the one cell performs all life functions.

modelAnswer: A unicellular organism is an organism made up of a single cell.
That one cell performs all the life functions of the organism.

items.followUp: What is a tissue, and how are cells arranged to form one?

rubric.why: The student identifies the cells that make up a tissue as similar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a tissue is made of similar cells.

rubric.why: The function of the grouped cells is stated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cells work together to perform a specific function.

modelAnswer: Tissue level is a level of organization in which similar cells are grouped together.
The cells work together to perform a specific function.

items.followUp: How do plasmodesmata help neighbouring plant cells?

rubric.why: The structure and location of plasmodesmata are identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing plasmodesmata as cytoplasmic strands passing through plant cell walls.

rubric.why: Their connecting role or function is stated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they connect neighbouring plant cells and allow communication or transport between them.

modelAnswer: Plasmodesmata are fine strands of cytoplasm that pass through the cell walls of adjacent plant cells.
They connect the cells and allow communication and transport between them.

items.followUp: State two ways biodiversity benefits people or ecosystems.

rubric.why: A valid resource or practical benefit of biodiversity is given.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one benefit such as providing food, medicines, or raw materials.

rubric.why: A valid ecological benefit of biodiversity is given.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that biodiversity helps maintain ecological balance or ecosystem stability.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity provides useful resources such as food, medicines, and raw materials.
It helps maintain ecological balance and stable ecosystems.

rubric.why: The chromosome-set numbers of diploid and haploid cells are correctly compared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that diploid cells have two sets (2n) and haploid cells have one set (n).

rubric.why: A correct example of where each cell type occurs is given.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying body (somatic) cells as diploid and gametes (sex cells) as haploid.

modelAnswer: Diploid cells have two sets of chromosomes (2n), whereas haploid cells have one set (n).
Body cells are generally diploid, while gametes (sex cells) are haploid.
